chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from one who narrated to him, from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'Indeed, among us are a group of Kurds, and they constantly come with trade, so we mix with them and conclude business with them.' He said: 'O Abu Rabi', do not mix with them, for the Kurds are a tribe from the tribes of the Jinn; Allah has lifted the veil from them, so do not mix with them.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the Kurds according to this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against social and commercial mixing with the Kurds, identifying them as a tribe of Jinn from whom the veil of humanity has been lifted, implying a distinct spiritual or physical nature. This classification reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of *al-Jinn al-Ins* (human-like Jinn), where specific tribes are believed to possess unique characteristics that warrant caution in daily interactions to preserve religious and social purity. The advice underscores the importance of discerning the nature of those with whom one engages in trade and community life, linking physical proximity to potential spiritual influence.
